hypothesis: BFSI/govtech document or voice workflows have urgent Indian-language pain and budget.
action: Interview 10 target buyers and rank workflows by volume, urgency, and incumbent dissatisfaction.
deliverable: ICP brief and ranked use-case scorecard
decision_rule: If fewer than 3 buyers name a near-term production trigger, change vertical or trigger.

hypothesis: Sarvam can win on quality or workflow simplicity on real Indian-language data.
action: Collect consented sample documents/audio and benchmark Sarvam against incumbent/open alternative.
metric: At least 100 documents or 10 hours audio across target languages
decision_rule: Continue only if one workflow shows a measurable win or materially lower integration cost.

hypothesis: A fixed-credit, fixed-scope pilot will convert evaluation into paid production intent.
action: Create pilot scope, acceptance criteria, pricing page/one-pager, and security FAQ.
decision_rule: If buyers reject paid conversion criteria, revise value metric and proof of ROI.

hypothesis: Targeted technical outreach beats broad awareness for the first wedge.
action: Contact 50 named accounts through founder-led outreach, partners, and relevant communities.
decision_rule: If reply/qualification is weak, switch trigger or partner source before adding spend.

hypothesis: The winning workflow can reach production acceptance within 2 weeks.
action: Launch 4 scoped pilots with weekly technical and buyer reviews.
decision_rule: Stop pilots with no data owner, acceptance metric, or production sponsor.

hypothesis: Usage revenue covers variable inference and support costs at the proposed package.
action: Instrument usage, infra cost, support hours, and outcome value by account.
deliverable: Account-level gross-margin sheet and pricing readout
metric: Cost and usage captured for all active pilots
decision_rule: Do not scale a use case with negative contribution after support cost.
